newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westpac Australia consumer sentiment index up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westpac Australia consumer sentiment index up.

text.p: Thoughts of another interest rate cut helped the Westpac-Melbourne Institute index of Australian consumer sentiment rise 1.1 points or 1.1 percent in July, arresting its recent decline, Westpac reported on Wednesday.

"The rise in the consumer index arrests the 5.8 percent decline in the index recorded in the preceding three months and is somewhat encouraging," Westpac Chief Economist Nigel Stapledon said in a commentary.

"The recovery of consumer sentiment rests heavily on a rise in confidence about the current state of household finances, reflecting a lagged response to the latest interest rate cut and reaction to the growing speculation of yet another cut to come in the near future," Stapledon said.
"The Reserve Bank is expected to validate that speculation with a rate cut sometime in the next few weeks," he said.

Conversely, reaction to the unexpectedly weak June employment figures was reflected in a more negative assessment by those interviewed about economic prospects for both the next 12 months and the next five years, he said.
"...This is holding back a revival in consumer spending," he said.

"The heightened sensitivity of consumer sentiment to employment prospects suggests that clear signs of improvement in the labour market could feed quickly into higher confidence, in turn leading to a recovery in consumer spending," he said.

"Particularly if the Reserve Bank does proceed with another rate cut, there is still a very good chance that a lift in consumer confidence and retail spending will be in place by Christmas 1997," Stapledon said.
The index, which is seasonally adjusted and reflects a balance between optimists and pessimists, rose to 101.1 from 100.0 in June.
The 1997 peak was 109.9 recorded in January.
The survey was based on interviews with 1,200 people between July 10 and 13.
